headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure between Dify and Gemini CLI.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write uploaded knowledge-base files and shares state via the Dify server datastore; Gemini CLI reads repo/user files and can use MCP tools. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Dify outputs are fed into Gemini CLI or vice versa. The pathway is not proven by docs, but it exists in default-style pairings.
conditions: IF Dify-generated content is copied into Gemini CLI prompts or files
IF Gemini CLI is configured to read Dify workspace artifacts as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces and never share prompt/output files
Add a manual review step before Gemini CLI consumes Dify artifacts
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed
Use a strict file naming convention for data vs instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment. Both have broad network egress, so sensitive material can flow from either agent into remote model backends or tools if the same workspace is reused. The shared-data path is plausible and not isolated by default.
conditions: IF the same directory contains both conversation artifacts and source code
IF either agent is pointed at files containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Keep Dify and Gemini CLI in separate directories
Remove secrets from shared folders before running either agent
Restrict network egress at the host or container level
Use throwaway test data for cross-agent workflows
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and both can spawn subprocesses; Gemini CLI also modifies git state, while Dify can run server-side code tools. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and cause irreversible repository corruption or lost work. The profiles explicitly show overlapping mutable access without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout or shared directory
IF Dify code tools and Gemini CLI run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in its own checkout
Pause one agent before the other edits files
Commit or stash before handing off between agents
Use filesystem-level locks for shared paths
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-managed concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit agent/workflow outputs, and Gemini CLI can act on files and shell commands. If Gemini CLI treats Dify output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Dify result can cascade into code edits, shell actions, or git changes. This interaction is plausible in default pairings and can produce downstream irreversible actions.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes Dify output without verification
IF Dify output is used to generate shell commands, patches, or git commits
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated commands
Compare Dify output against source files before acting
Use dry-run mode for any generated patch or command
Limit Gemini CLI to read-only analysis for Dify outputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment. If regulated data is placed into either system, retention and residency obligations can diverge because the profiles do not document matching compliance controls. The mismatch is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Dify conversation logs
IF the same regulated data is also processed by Gemini CLI without aligned retention controls
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Check retention settings before processing sensitive content
Delete conversation logs after use where permitted
Keep compliance-sensitive projects in separate environments
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
